title: toc-file-§5 load-bearing TOC lines unannotated outside # Core
cluster_summary: The root cause is upstream. WowAddonStandards/AUDIT.md step 4 limits the toc-file-§5 check to the # Core block and to *Setup.lua/core/Constants.lua, and the denominator paragraph in standards/standards/toc-file.md:154-157 makes the same narrowing. The rule itself (toc-file.md:133) covers every position in the listing. That gap is why load-bearing settings\ and modules\ positions in AbsorbTracker, LootHistory and ConsumableMaster went unflagged. Fix both upstream texts once (WowAddonStandards). Then annotate the per-repo TOC lines locally: these are comment-only, latent MUST breaches with no runtime change, so do them as one commit per addon. The upstream fix does not make them moot.

verdicts.assessment: Schema.lua publishes NS.SchemaRuntime and NS.RegisterSchemaRows, which OptionsSetup and General resolve at file load. TOC :83 is bare, which is a real but latent toc-file-§5 MUST breach that a one-line comment fixes.
verdicts.remediation: Add a LOAD-BEARING comment above AbsorbTracker.toc:83 naming NS.SchemaRuntime (read at load by OptionsSetup) and NS.RegisterSchemaRows (called at load by General). Use the same commit as AT-A-05.

verdicts.assessment: NS.Helpers is captured as a file-scope upvalue by UnitPanel, About, General and Appearance. If they loaded earlier they would capture nil and fail later, inside callbacks, so this is the silent failure mode the rule targets. The fix is comment-only.
verdicts.remediation: Add a LOAD-BEARING comment above AbsorbTracker.toc:85 naming NS.Helpers and its file-scope consumers. Optionally add one CONVENTIONAL line for the remaining settings positions. Same commit as AT-A-04.

verdicts.assessment: Verified: the CoreSetup annotation (ConsumableMaster.toc:95-97) names only SlashCommands, while SlashDump.lua:16 also captures KCM.Say at file scope. SlashDump.lua:15 also names the wrong seam (core/Constants.lua). Both fixes are comment-only.
verdicts.remediation: Extend the CoreSetup TOC comment to name core\SlashDump.lua and core\SlashCommands.lua as file-scope consumers of KCM.Say. Correct core/SlashDump.lua:15 to cite core/CoreSetup.lua.

verdicts.assessment: This is only the SHOULD half of §5. The seed files are verifiably conventional (no file-scope read of KCM.Categories), and nothing breaks. The marker is a documentary nicety.
verdicts.remediation: If touched in the CM-A-03 commit, add one CONVENTIONAL comment line after the defaults\Profile.lua block covering Categories.lua and the Defaults_*.lua seed files.

verdicts.assessment: Escrow appends to NS.Reconciler.SCAN_STEPS/PLAN_STEPS at file load, and TOC :102 is bare. This is a latent MUST breach and the root of LH-A-15..18. Annotate it rather than take the LH-82 refactor, which is churn far out of proportion to a doc gap.
verdicts.remediation: Add a LOAD-BEARING comment above LootHistory.toc:102 (modules\Reconciler.lua must be above, because Escrow appends to its SCAN_STEPS/PLAN_STEPS at load). Use one commit for the whole # Modules/# Settings group, together with LH-A-15/16/17/18.

verdicts.assessment: AnalyticsCharts.lua:2 binds NS.Analytics without a guard and writes into it at load, so the position is load-bearing. The constraint is that at least one of AnalyticsFormat/Analytics/AnalyticsLedger must load above it, not Analytics.lua specifically.
verdicts.remediation: In the LH-A-01 commit, annotate LootHistory.toc:112, saying that NS.Analytics must already exist (created by AnalyticsFormat/Analytics above). Alternatively add 'NS.Analytics = NS.Analytics or {}' to AnalyticsCharts.lua:2 and mark the position conventional.

verdicts.assessment: Timeline.lua reads TM.TOTAL from NS.TimelineModel at file scope, so it is a load-bearing position with a bare TOC line. The fix is a trivial comment.
verdicts.remediation: In the LH-A-01 commit, annotate LootHistory.toc:116 (modules\TimelineModel.lua must be above, because Timeline reads TM.TOTAL at load).

verdicts.assessment: settings/Panel.lua:961 reads NS.Schema.MASTER_GROUP/MasterAfterGroup at file scope, and TOC :131 is bare. This is a latent MUST breach.
verdicts.remediation: In the LH-A-01 commit, annotate LootHistory.toc:131 (settings\Schema.lua must be above, because Panel reads MASTER_GROUP/MasterAfterGroup at load).

verdicts.assessment: The conventional marker on its own is a SHOULD. However, the header '(Attribution before Collector)' asserts a load-order dependency that does not exist, because Collector reaches NS.Attribution only inside functions, and that misleads maintainers. It costs nothing in the LH-A-01 commit.
verdicts.remediation: In the LH-A-01 commit, drop the '(Attribution before Collector)' parenthesis from LootHistory.toc:94 and add one CONVENTIONAL line covering the modules\ positions that are not annotated as load-bearing.

verdicts.assessment: This is the root cause of the cluster. Verified: AUDIT.md step 4 (around line 402) scopes the check to the # Core block and to *Setup.lua/core/Constants.lua, and standards/standards/toc-file.md:154-157 (denominator paragraph) has the same narrowing, while toc-file.md:133 covers every position. Unless both are widened, future audits will keep missing settings\ and modules\ seams. The fix lands in WowAddonStandards, not AbsorbTracker.
verdicts.remediation: In WowAddonStandards, widen AUDIT.md step 4 from 'In the # Core block' to every position in the listing. Also widen the toc-file.md denominator paragraph so load-bearing positions are established by reading every listed file that binds, reads or writes an NS member at file scope, including modules\ and settings\ files, not only *Setup.lua and core\Constants.lua. Add the standard's changelog/version ripple as that repo's CLAUDE.md requires.
